table_assessment.assessment_notes: Exact review confirms a three-part patient/caregiver education and professional-behaviour table spanning medication, devices, self-care, lifestyle, monitoring, psychosocial support, and referral. It is primarily other normative clinical instruction, not a medication-recommendation table. Concrete patient goals and every professional imperative are annotated; the blank first row of part 2 inherits Sleep and breathing, and the blank first row of part 3 inherits Psychological issues. Mixed scope and advice that changes during acute decompensation or toward end-of-life prevent table-example readiness.

text_units.verbatim_text: Provide tailored information.

entities.surface_form: when there is a change in the clinical condition

normative_assertions.notes: The full source timing list, including treatment-option decision making, is preserved verbatim.

text_units.verbatim_text: Sensitively communicate information on prognosis at time of diagnosis, during decision making about treatment options, when there is a change in the clinical condition and whenever the patient requests.

normative_assertions.notes: Medication context is inherited from the row heading.

text_units.verbatim_text: Provide written and oral information on indication, benefits, dosing, effects and side effects. Discuss practical issues such as optimal time-schedule, what to do in case of a missed dose etc. Discuss possible barriers for medication taking. Advise on support aids such as dosette box, electronic reminders etc. when appropriate. 320

entities.surface_form: situations where the device might be deactivated or explanted

normative_assertions.notes: COUNSEL represents patient/caregiver involvement in shared decision making.

text_units.verbatim_text: Provide written and oral information about the importance and expectations of implanted devices, and possible ways of follow-up (remote monitoring). Discuss expectations and any possible impact on driving. Clearly identify situations where the device might be deactivated or explanted. Involve patient and caregiver in decision making.

header_path: Goal for the patient and caregiver

normative_assertions.notes: Concrete patient action stated as a table goal.
source_trigger_texts: Goal for the patient and caregiver
Goal for the patient and caregiver

text_units.verbatim_text: To undertake regular exercise and be physically active. To be able to adapt physical activity to symptom status and personal circumstances.

normative_assertions.notes: The same discussion also covers opportunities, preserved in verbatim text.

text_units.verbatim_text: Advise on exercise that recognizes physical and functional limitations, such as frailty, comorbidities. Refer to exercise programme or other activity modes. Discuss possible barriers, side-effects and opportunities.
Review sleep history. Advise and discuss the importance of good sleep and provide advice on 'sleep health' (including timing of diuretics).

header_path: Education topic: Sleep and breathing (continued from source part 1, row 9)

normative_assertions.notes: The inherited topic is explicit in header_path.

text_units.verbatim_text: Consider and carefully discuss the benefits and deleterious effects of sleep medication.

entities.surface_form: periods of high heat/humidity and/or nausea/vomiting

header_path: Goal for the patient and caregiver

normative_assertions.notes: Concrete fluid-intake goal.
Fluid restriction is optional at the stated source-native amount.
Applies where fluids are restricted and during the stated periods.

text_units.verbatim_text: To avoid large volumes of fluid intake. A fluid restriction of 1.5–2 L/day may be considered in patients with severe HF/hyponatraemia to relieve symptoms and congestion. To avoid dehydration: where fluids are restricted, increase intake during periods of high heat/humidity and/or nausea/vomiting.

entities.surface_form: advantages and disadvantages of fluid restriction

normative_assertions.notes: Nausea/vomiting is also an explicit condition in the verbatim source.

text_units.verbatim_text: Provide information and discuss the advantages and disadvantages of fluid restriction. Advise to adapt fluid intake to weight, and in times of high heat and humidity, nausea/vomiting. Adjust advice during periods of acute decompensation and consider altering this advice towards end-of-life.

header_path: Goal for the patient and caregiver

normative_assertions.notes: The schema has no eating/diet-specific operation.
source_trigger_texts: Goal for the patient and caregiver

normative_assertions.notes: Source threshold is preserved verbatim.
The schema has no maintain-weight operation.

text_units.verbatim_text: To be able to prevent malnutrition and know how to eat healthily, avoiding excessive salt intake (>5 g/day) and maintaining a healthy body weight.

normative_assertions.notes: The discussion also explicitly covers the roles of salt and micronutrients.
Explicit absence of a clear role is kept distinct from the counselling instruction.

text_units.verbatim_text: Discuss current food intake, role of salt, role of micronutrients. Discuss the need for supplementing in case of nutrient deficiencies but there is no clear role for routine micronutrient supplementation. 321 Discuss maintaining a healthy body weight.

header_path: Goal for the patient and caregiver

normative_assertions.notes: Abstinence is especially directed for alcohol-induced cardiomyopathy.

text_units.verbatim_text: To be able to abstain from or avoid excessive alcohol intake, especially for alcohol-induced CMP. To restrict alcohol according to CV prevention guidelines.

normative_assertions.notes: Sex-specific source thresholds are preserved without reinterpretation.

text_units.verbatim_text: Tailor alcohol advice to aetiology of HF; e.g. abstinence in alcoholic CMP. Inform and discuss alcohol intake according to CV prevention guidelines (2 units per day in men or 1 unit per day in women) a.

entities.surface_form: immunization for influenza and pneumococcal disease

header_path: Goal for the patient and caregiver

normative_assertions.notes: The source states immunization need as a patient education goal.

text_units.verbatim_text: To be aware of the need for immunization for influenza and pneumococcal disease.
Discuss benefits and possible barriers. Advise on local immunization practice.

header_path: Education topic: Smoking and recreational drugs
Goal for the patient and caregiver

normative_assertions.notes: Direct imperative includes e-cigarettes and recreational drugs.

text_units.verbatim_text: To be aware of the consequences for health of smoking and use of recreational drugs. Stop smoking (including e-cigarettes) and taking recreational drugs.

entities.surface_form: patient wishes to stop smoking or taking drugs

header_path: Education topic: Smoking and recreational drugs

text_units.verbatim_text: Inform, discuss and help in decision making. Refer for specialist advice for smoking cessation and drug withdrawal and replacement therapy. Consider referral for cognitive behavioural theory and psychological support if patient wishes to stop smoking or taking drugs.

entities.surface_form: practical issues related to long haul travel, staying abroad, exposure to sun (amiodarone effects), high humidity or heat (dehydration), and high altitude (oxygenation)

normative_assertions.notes: All luggage, medication-list, device-card, and treating-centre details remain in the verbatim text.

text_units.verbatim_text: Inform and discuss practical issues related to long haul travel, staying abroad, exposure to sun (amiodarone effects), high humidity or heat (dehydration), and high altitude (oxygenation). Provide practical advice related to travel with medication/devices (keep medicines in hand luggage, have a list with medication, device name/card and treating centres). Inform about local/national/international regulation related to driving.

header_path: Goal for the patient and caregiver

normative_assertions.notes: Concrete patient goal; the second sentence is an awareness objective rather than a separate act.
source_trigger_texts: Goal for the patient and caregiver

text_units.verbatim_text: To be able to resume or adapt sexual activity according to physical capacity. To recognize possible problems with sexual activity and their relationship with HF or its treatment.

factual_relations.notes: The source separately asserts safety for the stated stable-HF population.

normative_assertions.notes: The factual safety claim is represented separately below.

text_units.verbatim_text: Inform and discuss that sexual activity is safe for stable HF patients. Provide advice on eliminating factors predisposing to sexual problems. Discuss and provide available pharmacological treatment for sexual problems. Refer to specialist for sexual counselling when necessary.

entities.surface_form: react adequately to change in signs and symptoms

header_path: Education topic: Symptom monitoring and symptom self-management
Goal for the patient and caregiver

normative_assertions.notes: No schema operation specifically represents self-management reaction.
No schema operation specifically represents contacting a clinician.

text_units.verbatim_text: Monitor and recognize change in signs and symptoms. Being able to react adequately to change in signs and symptoms. Know how and when to contact a healthcare professional.

header_path: Education topic: Symptom monitoring and symptom self-management

normative_assertions.notes: The three alternative symptom/weight conditions and exact threshold are retained.
The schema has no contact/alert operation.

text_units.verbatim_text: Provide individualized information to support self-management such as: In the case of increasing dyspnoea or oedema or a sudden unexpected weight gain of >2 kg in 3 days, patients may increase their diuretic dose and/or alert their healthcare team.

entities.surface_form: information on disease, treatment options and self-care

normative_assertions.notes: The treatment modality is not specified, so no more specific operation is inferred.

text_units.verbatim_text: Regularly communicate information on disease, treatment options and self-care. Regularly discuss the need for support. Treat or referral to specialist for psychological support when necessary.

Goal for the patient and caregiver

text_units.verbatim_text: To recognise that the carer or family members may be greatly affected and need to seek help.
